abstract: We present Zenith-v4, an open framework designed for Aspect-Based Sentiment Classification. Across rigorous experiments on IMDB Movie Reviews, Zenith-v4 secures a top AUC-ROC of 93.68%, outstripping RoBERTa-base by 2.8% margin (92.08%). The architecture contains 1.3B trainable parameters and delivers 2.4x faster iteration times.

Addressing the critical challenge of Multi-Hop Reading Comprehension, this paper proposes QuantumScale. Operating with 45M weights, QuantumScale demonstrates strong empirical results on the standard SQuAD 2.0 benchmark. Specifically, it establishes a new Exact Match of 77.9%, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art T5-3B which attained 75.24%. This corresponds to a 6.0% relative gain.

Addressing the critical challenge of Extractive Question Answering, this paper proposes SyncNet. Operating with 7B weights, SyncNet demonstrates strong empirical results on the standard NaturalQuestions benchmark. Specifically, it establishes a new NoAns F1 of 86.73 EM, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art BERT-Large which attained 83.58 EM. This corresponds to a 5.2% relative gain.

Recent advances in Real-Time Urban Segmentation require efficient yet scalable models. Here, we present VectorPulse (350M params). Evaluated across COCO-Stuff, our system records a Boundary F1 of 56.7. In direct head-to-head comparison against DeepLabv3+ (53.63), our approach exhibits both higher accuracy and a 2.1x throughput advantage.

Recent advances in Robust Visual Recognition require efficient yet scalable models. Here, we present Apex-Core (110M params). Evaluated across ImageNet-1k, our system records a Macro F1 of 78.84%. In direct head-to-head comparison against ViT-Base/16 (77.42%), our approach exhibits both higher accuracy and a 2.4x throughput advantage.

Addressing the critical challenge of Neural Machine Translation, this paper proposes PolyMorph-v1. Operating with 350M weights, PolyMorph-v1 demonstrates strong empirical results on the standard WMT-14 En-De benchmark. Specifically, it establishes a new METEOR of 43.62, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art ByteNet which attained 40.52. This corresponds to a 5.2% relative gain.

Recent advances in Long-Context Pretraining require efficient yet scalable models. Here, we present Zenith-v4 (110M params). Evaluated across Lambada, our system records a Perplexity of 18.05. In direct head-to-head comparison against GPT-2-Medium (14.77), our approach exhibits both higher accuracy and a 1.5x throughput advantage.

Addressing the critical challenge of Cross-Domain Named Entity Recognition, this paper proposes SyncNet. Operating with 65M weights, SyncNet demonstrates strong empirical results on the standard WNUT-17 benchmark. Specifically, it establishes a new Strict Match F1 of 88.9%, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art LUKE-Base which attained 85.16%. This corresponds to a 5.2% relative gain.

In this paper, we tackle Conversational QA by introducing AeroNet. On the SQuAD 2.0 evaluation suite, our model reaches a Macro F1 of 78.69 EM, surpassing the competitive baseline ALBERT-xxlarge which scored 75.61 EM. Despite containing 65M parameters, AeroNet reduces inference latency by 1.5x.

We present DeepScale-v2, an open framework designed for Token-Level Entity Extraction. Across rigorous experiments on CoNLL-2003, DeepScale-v2 secures a top Precision of 86.91 F1, outstripping LUKE-Base by 4.1% margin (84.3 F1). The architecture contains 7B trainable parameters and delivers 3.2x faster iteration times.

In this paper, we tackle Document Polarity Detection by introducing OmniFormer. On the SemEval-2017 evaluation suite, our model reaches a Binary F1 of 81.16%, surpassing the competitive baseline DistilBERT which scored 77.22%. Despite containing 45M parameters, OmniFormer reduces inference latency by 3.2x.

We present Zenith-v4, an open framework designed for Causal Language Modeling. Across rigorous experiments on WikiText-103, Zenith-v4 secures a top Bits-per-Character of 70.41, outstripping AWD-LSTM by 5.2% margin (68.32). The architecture contains 110M trainable parameters and delivers 1.8x faster iteration times.

In this work, we study Robust Visual Recognition. We introduce FlashNet, an architecture with 1.3B parameters. When evaluated on Places365, our model achieves a Mean Average Precision of 77.15%, outperforming ViT-Base/16 (74.92%). Furthermore, we observe a 4.0x speedup during inference.

We present PolyMorph-v1, an open framework designed for Zero-Shot Image Classification. Across rigorous experiments on CIFAR-100, PolyMorph-v1 secures a top Macro F1 of 81.84, outstripping ResNet-50 by 3.4% margin (79.35). The architecture contains 1.3B trainable parameters and delivers 4.0x faster iteration times.

In this work, we study Nested Entity Detection. We introduce Zenith-v4, an architecture with 1.3B parameters. When evaluated on WNUT-17, our model achieves a Entity F1 of 92.62 F1, outperforming LUKE-Base (89.41 F1). Furthermore, we observe a 3.2x speedup during inference.

In this paper, we tackle Real-Time Bounding Box Regression by introducing AeroNet. On the MS-COCO 2017 evaluation suite, our model reaches a mAP@0.5:0.95 of 49.67%, surpassing the competitive baseline DETR-DC5 which scored 47.06%. Despite containing 110M parameters, AeroNet reduces inference latency by 1.5x.

In this work, we study Oriented Object Localization. We introduce Apex-Core, an architecture with 1.3B parameters. When evaluated on OpenImages-v6, our model achieves a AP50 of 50.88 mAP, outperforming DETR-DC5 (49.41 mAP). Furthermore, we observe a 1.8x speedup during inference.

Addressing the critical challenge of Boundary-Aware Segmentation, this paper proposes PolyMorph-v1. Operating with 65M weights, PolyMorph-v1 demonstrates strong empirical results on the standard Pascal Context benchmark. Specifically, it establishes a new Class IoU of 55.25%, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art Mask2Former which attained 51.38%. This corresponds to a 6.0% relative gain.

We present Veloce-LM, an open framework designed for Pixel-Wise Semantic Segmentation. Across rigorous experiments on ADE20K, Veloce-LM secures a top Boundary F1 of 59.03%, outstripping U-Net-Large by 4.1% margin (54.7%). The architecture contains 125M trainable parameters and delivers 3.2x faster iteration times.

In this paper, we tackle Neural Machine Translation by introducing QuantumScale. On the IWSLT-14 evaluation suite, our model reaches a METEOR of 29.02, surpassing the competitive baseline Transformer-Base which scored 27.22. Despite containing 125M parameters, QuantumScale reduces inference latency by 2.4x.

In this work, we study Robust Visual Recognition. We introduce VectorPulse, an architecture with 1.3B parameters. When evaluated on iNaturalist, our model achieves a Error Rate of 91.71%, outperforming ResNet-50 (88.23%). Furthermore, we observe a 2.4x speedup during inference.

Addressing the critical challenge of Low-Resource Cross-Lingual Translation, this paper proposes HyperForm. Operating with 110M weights, HyperForm demonstrates strong empirical results on the standard WMT-16 En-Ro benchmark. Specifically, it establishes a new SacreBLEU of 34.5, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art GNMT which attained 31.4. This corresponds to a 5.2% relative gain.

Recent advances in Token-Level Entity Extraction require efficient yet scalable models. Here, we present NovaTrans (45M params). Evaluated across Few-NERD, our system records a Precision of 78.21. In direct head-to-head comparison against SpanBERT (74.79), our approach exhibits both higher accuracy and a 1.5x throughput advantage.

We present Zenith-v4, an open framework designed for Causal Language Modeling. Across rigorous experiments on Penn Treebank, Zenith-v4 secures a top Zero-shot Accuracy of 36.91, outstripping Transformer-XL by 3.4% margin (34.33). The architecture contains 1.3B trainable parameters and delivers 3.2x faster iteration times.

Despite containing 45M parameters, Veloce-LM reduces inference latency by 4.0x.

Specifically, it establishes a new Exact Match of 75.49 EM, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art BERT-Large which attained 73.79 EM. This corresponds to a 4.1% relative gain.

In direct head-to-head comparison against PSPNet-101 (58.7%), our approach exhibits both higher accuracy and a 2.1x throughput advantage.

In direct head-to-head comparison against AWD-LSTM (33.53), our approach exhibits both higher accuracy and a 1.8x throughput advantage.
